name: docstring-comment-style
description: Docstring and comment content rules for Tactics2D project: document what code does and how to use it, not how it was written
principle: Docstrings and comments describe the interface: what the code does and how to call it. Implementation reasoning, clever tricks, and history do not belong in them.

include: One-line summary of what the callable does, in imperative mood
Returns: meaning of the returned value
exclude: Why the implementation was written this way
Notes comparing against other implementations, frameworks, or papers
Bug history, version notes, migration notes
Performance anecdotes (caching, vectorization, memory) unless they change the API

include: Non-obvious preconditions, invariants, and units at the point of use
Why a caller must use the API in a particular order (usage constraints)
Inline '# default ...' labels for module-level constants
exclude: Restating what the next line of code already says
Explaining a trick, hack, or workaround and its rationale
Narrating design decisions, trade-offs, or 'we do X so that Y'
Referencing a paper, upstream repo, or PR as justification

blockCommentLimit.message: A comment block longer than 2 lines is almost always explaining rationale; move it to a commit message, PR description, or docs/ page.

actions.message: Docstrings and comments should describe what the code does and how to use it (summary + Args/Returns/Raises). Do not explain implementation reasoning or clever tricks.
When adding a docstring or comment, ask: does a caller need this to use the code correctly? If it only explains how the code was written, delete it. Keep comment blocks to 1-2 lines.
